args.name: exoDecruncher

args.name: exoDecruncher

args.name: decruncherCopyHead
args.comment: Not code: the copy loop at $0813 walks a fixed offset, so these four bytes ride along from $50A3-$50A6. $FC-$FF are the decruncher zero-page workspace and are overwritten before use.

args.name: crunchedStream
args.comment: Exomizer-crunched payload. Read BACKWARDS: the byte fetch at $011F is a self-modifying LDA $5068 whose operand at $0120/$0121 is decremented, so the stream runs from $5067 down. At run time it continues below this into $07E7-$081E, which the loader copies in from $516E because the BASIC stub occupies those addresses in the file.

args.name: decruncherImage
args.comment: Image of the decruncher, copied to $00FC-$01xx by the loop at $0813 and executed there, never here. See the exoDecruncher region at $0100.

args.name: decruncherTablesImage
args.comment: Image of the two 3-byte tables the decruncher indexes as $01C0,Y and $01C3,Y with Y=1..3 (bit counts 2,4,4 and offsets $30,$20,$10).

args.name: crunchHeadStash
args.comment: The first 56 bytes of the crunched stream, held here because the BASIC stub and SYS code occupy $0801-$081E in the file. $5068 copies $516E-$51A5 to $07E7-$081E before decrunching starts.

args.name: exoTables
args.comment: Two 3-byte tables, indexed as $01C0,Y and $01C3,Y with Y=1..3.

args.name: copyOverrun
args.comment: Not part of the decruncher. The relocation loop at $0813 takes its count from TSX rather than a fixed length, so it drags whatever follows the decruncher in the file ($516E onward, the stashed crunch head) up to here. Never read; harmless because the stack pointer sits above it.

args.description: Revenge of the Mutant Camels (Llamasoft, 1984), from revenge-of-the-mutant-camels.d64, file "revenge fixed" (75 blocks, loads $0801-$51A6). The disk holds a CRUNCHED program: only ~330 bytes of it are code. BASIC line 20 SYS 2061 enters at $080D, which relocates an Exomizer 2 decruncher from $50A4 to $0100 and jumps to $5068; that builds the Huffman-ish tables at $0333/$0367/$039B, decrunches the stream at $07E7-$5067 (read backwards from $5067), and jumps to $C065. The decruncher is disassembled at its true addresses through a second, raw layer over the same bytes. The decrunched program is held in a third layer, produced by running the loader in a 6502 interpreter outside re64, because no tool here can execute one.

args.comment: Exomizer 2 sfx decruncher, as it exists at run time. args.name: spriteAnimTable

args.name: spriteSample

args.name: Variables1F00

comments.text:
Boot chain, start to finish:
  $0801  BASIC line 20 SYS 2061
  $080D  LDY #$38, SEI, INC $01 ($37 -> $38, so $D000-$DFFF is RAM), TSX
  $0813  copy $50A3+X -> $00FC+X down to X=1 - the decruncher, landing here
  $081C  JMP $5068
  $5068  copy $516E-$51A5 -> $07E7-$081E: the head of the crunched stream,
         which could not be stored there in the file because the BASIC stub
         occupies those addresses
  $5071  build the three decode tables at $0333/$0367/$039B, 52 entries
  $50A1  JMP $013E, the decrunch loop here
  $01BB  DEC $01 back to $37, CLI, JMP $C065
The stream runs $07E7-$5067 and is read BACKWARDS: the fetch at $011F is a
self-modifying LDA whose operand at $0120/$0121 is decremented each time.
loading stripe: bank I/O in for one store to colour RAM
operand at $0120/$0121 counts down from $5068

Entry after decrunching - the address the loader jumps to, and not where the
program loads. LOAD "ATTACK MUTANT.HI" ,8 to $5E00 (secondary address 0, so
the address in X/Y is used), then JMP $8A3C into the game proper.
Its sibling at $C082 saves the same buffer back as "@:ATTACK MUTANT.HI".

Installs the game interrupts: IRQ -> $88D5 via $0314, NMI -> $88D4 via $0318,
and $0291 = $80. Compare $C0B9, which puts the KERNAL default $EA31 back.
three-way dispatch; see the jumptable at $9933

18KB of graphics before the first instruction. Read as C64 sprites it draws
camels - see the sample at $3000. Marked data on that evidence plus the fact
that no decoded instruction transfers control into it; if something reaches it
by a route a static walk cannot follow, that would show up as a hole here.

Data between the two code banks. From about $5900 it is note/duration byte
pairs, around $6800 map or screen tables, around $7C00 screen-code text.

args.name: MusicData1
args.comment: Note/duration byte pairs; the intro tune. Read only through pointers, so no absolute instruction names it.

args.name: IntroCredits
args.comment: The scrolling attract-mode text, in screen codes. Names the author: THIS PROGRAM WAS WRITTEN OVER A TWO MONTH PERIOD BY JEFF MINTER, and the music arranger, JAMES LISNEY.

args.name: HiScoreTableAndStatusLine
args.comment: Default hi-score table plus the two status-line templates. $5E00-$5ECF is what Start loads over from the disk file ATTACK MUTANT.HI and what SaveHiScoreAndRestart writes back (SETNAM at $C09C, save range from ($FB)=$5E00 to $5ED0).

args.name: WaveDescriptors
args.comment: The 42 attack waves. A screen-code name field recurs on an exact 200-byte stride from $67A0 (ASSORTED EASY AVIAN ALIENS) to $8618 (ZAPSTARS III) -- 40 of them, the other two apparently blank. The record base and the rest of the layout are not established; only the stride and the name offset are evidence.

args.name: UninitialisedBuffer
args.comment: 7936 bytes, every one of them zero in the decrunched image, and no instruction anywhere refers to the span by absolute address. Working RAM the program fills at run time, not content.

args.name: LoaderFilenames
args.comment: The two PETSCII filenames the startup code passes to SETNAM: ATTACK MUTANT.HI at $C102 for the load, @:ATTACK MUTANT.HI at $C100 for the save-with-replace.

args.name: objectTables
args.comment: Not graphics: parallel per-object arrays on a 16-byte stride, indexed by X. Several are addressed one low ($1F3F,X for the table at $1F40) because the object index is 1-based.

args.name: SidNoteTable
args.comment: Rising byte sequence that wraps every octave -- the SID frequency table. Read only through indexed pointers.

args.name: StatusLineTemplate
args.comment: PETSCII, not screen codes -- $8A44 reads it with LDA dat_90F8,X / AND #$3F / STA $5F00,X, and that mask is exactly the PETSCII-to-screen-code conversion for uppercase.

args.description:
Revenge of the Mutant Camels (Llamasoft / Jeff Minter, 1984), C64, built from revenge-of-the-mutant-camels.d64.

The disk holds two files: REVENGE FIXED (75 blocks) and ATTACK MUTANT.HI (1 block, the hi-score save). REVENGE FIXED loads to $0801-$51A6, and almost all of it is compressed: a BASIC stub SYS 2061 runs an Exomizer 2 self-extractor which unpacks 47391 bytes over $0800-$C11E and jumps to $C065 -- an address the file never loads into. Static analysis of the file as it comes off the disk reaches 141 instructions and can reach no more, because the program is not in the file in executable form.

Layer 2 is that decrunched image. It was produced by running the game s own loader: extract REVENGE FIXED from the .d64, execute from $080D in a 6502 interpreter with $01 banking modelled and $D000-$DFFF treated as I/O, and stop at the JMP $C065 the decruncher ends with. 1,768,814 instructions later every byte of $0800-$C11E has been written, with no gaps. The scripts are run/extract-d64.cjs and run/run6502.cjs.

Memory map as it runs: VIC bank 0, video matrix $0400, character base $2000 (from $8AE7 STA $D018 with #$18). $0800-$1EFF and $2800-$4FFF graphics; $1F00-$1FFF variables; $5000-$5847 and $87FE-$9FEE and $C000-$C0CA code; $5848-$65FF music and text; $6600-$87FD the 42 attack-wave descriptors on a 200-byte stride; $A100-$BFFF working RAM, all zero as loaded.

Layer 0 (the crunched file) is kept as provenance and is fully shadowed by layer 2 above $0800. Layer 1 is the decruncher at the address it actually runs at, $0100-$01BF, reconstructed from the copy loop at $0813.

comments.text:
Four parallel sprite tables on a 16-byte stride, indexed 1-based, so every read
is one below the base: $1F40 X, $1F50 Y, $1F60 colour (copied to $D027,X),
$1F70 shape pointer (copied to $07F8,X). Their extents are declared as 15 and
not 16 on purpose: at 16, $1F4F falls inside spriteXPos and renders as
"spriteXPos + $000F" instead of "spriteYPos-1", which is the same address and
the wrong statement about what the code means.

Sprite N: copy X, Y, colour and shape pointer out of the object tables into the
VIC registers. Y = (X-1)*2 indexes $D000/$D001 in pairs; bit 7 of the colour
byte means "animate", and is incremented in place with the flag kept.

THE REAL ENTRY POINT.

The file on disk loads to $0801-$51A6 and nothing in it lives here. The chain: BASIC line 10 SYS 2061 -> $080D copies 200-odd bytes from $50A4 down into $00FD-$01F2 and jumps to $5068, which builds the Exomizer tables at $0334/$0368/$039C and enters the decruncher at $013E; the decruncher unpacks $0800-$C11E from the backwards stream ending at $5067 and finishes with DEC $01 / CLI / JMP $C065 at $01BB.

With only the image address $0800 as an entry point, 14 instructions decode. With this one, 2495.
logical file 0, device 8, secondary 0
loads ATTACK MUTANT.HI to $5E00
into the game proper
Game over: re-init the machine, restore the KERNAL IRQ, then SAVE $5E00-$5ED0 back to the disk as @:ATTACK MUTANT.HI and restart. Reached by a computed jump; no absolute reference points here.
Main. Zeroes the game state in zero page, installs the raster interrupt, fills the screen with character $28 and colour $06, then falls into the attract/title sequence.

Installs the interrupt handlers: CINV -> $88D5 (raster), NMINV -> $88D4 (which is a bare RTI, so RESTORE is dead), $0291 = $80 to lock the character set, RASTER = $60, IRQMASK = $81 (raster IRQ on), and opens the SID with volume 15.
NMI handler: a single RTI. Standard protection against RESTORE.
$18 = video matrix $0400, character base $2000 -- and nothing writes $DD00, so VIC bank 0

get_bits: reads X bits from the crunched stream into A (low) and $9F (high). $0108 is get_bit, which refills from the byte at the self-modified LDA at $011F, whose operand at $0120/$0121 walks backwards from $5068.

comments.text: Writes YXPAND ($D017), SPMC ($D01C) and XXPAND ($D01D) -- per-sprite expand and multicolour flags -- from a bit built out of $1F98/$1F99 and $32.
Writes six screen cells 40 bytes apart ($0657, $067F, $06A7, $06CF, $06F7, $071F) and the matching colour RAM ($DA57 ...), i.e. one column of six rows. routine_effects names all twelve addresses.
Reads the two status-line buffers at $5F00 and $5F80 and their three-byte fields at +$30 and +$B0. $539B is the write side, same layout.

args.text: Built camels-1 from the .d64. The file on disk is Exomizer-crunched: static analysis of it tops out at 141 instructions. Ran the game own loader in a 6502 interpreter, snapshotted $0800-$C11E, and added it as layer 2. Real entry is $C065, from the DEC $01 / CLI / JMP at the end of the decruncher. 14 instructions from the image load address alone, 3452 now. Memory map and evidence are in the project description and in comments at $C065, $886F, $8AE7.
